process_area.title: Micro-Fulfillment Daily Pick / Pack / Dispatch Operations

fields.Frequency: 6–12 wave releases per day per dark store
fields.Participants: Dark Store Shift Supervisor, WMS, Pickers, Packers, Dispatch
fields.Trigger: Continuous order intake; cut-off windows; batch release schedule
fields.Volume: ~50–400 orders per wave; ~1,000–5,000 lines/day per dark store

workflows.name: Dark Store Order Wave Planning & Batch Release

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-route of "route/zone, and item overlap" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-review of "reviews proposed wave" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-generate of "prints pick labels / pushes to RF guns / dispatches goods-to-person bins" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-509 (ensure controlled execution — Micro-Fulfillment Daily Pick / Pack / Dispatch Operations (PA-93.2).)
- operational: atomic reservation and real-time sync to ecommerce (links to VS-10)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Oversell risk**: Wave reserved against stale inventory; mitigated by atomic reservation and real-time sync to ecommerce (links to VS-10)
System Touchpoints: - WMS wave engine; OMS/order reservation (links to VS-60/VS-10); inventory (links to VS-05)

steps.activity: WMS continuously aggregates eligible orders (links to VS-60) into a wave plan: group by SLA tier (same-day, next-day, BOPIS), cut-off, dispatch route/zone, and item overlap; respects promised time and rider/3PL capacity
Dark Store Shift Supervisor reviews proposed wave: volume vs. staffing, automation availability, hot-orders, known stockouts/substitutes; adjusts wave size and releases batch to pick

System reserves inventory against wave (atomic reservation to prevent oversell), prints pick labels / pushes to RF guns / dispatches goods-to-person bins; flags short-pick candidates for substitute approval

fields.Participants: Pickers, Dark Store Shift Supervisor, Automation (if MFC)

workflows.name: Multi-Order Batch Picking & RF/Automation-Guided Walk Optimization

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-scan of "scans bin and item at each pick face" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-validate of "validates scan-to-tote to prevent wrong-order placement" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-log of "triggers substitute suggestion" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-77 (ensure dark-store order accuracy & dispatch control.)
- operational: scan-to-tote, weight-check at pack station, and picker accuracy KPI
Pain Points / Risks: - **Pick accuracy**: Mis-pick drives customer complaint and shrink; mitigated by scan-to-tote, weight-check at pack station, and picker accuracy KPI
System Touchpoints: - WMS pick engine; RF/voice/automation control; substitute logic (links to VS-01)
Time Estimate: - Per wave; ~20–40 min/wave depending on size

steps.activity: Picker follows RF/automation-guided walk sequence (optimized for shortest path / goods-to-person bin delivery); scans bin and item at each pick face; confirms quantity against pick label/tote
Multi-order batch pick: picker places each picked line into the correct customer tote/order partition (sort-while-picking); system validates scan-to-tote to prevent wrong-order placement

On short-pick (stockout, damaged): picker marks reason code in WMS; system triggers substitute suggestion (links to VS-01 substitute logic) or short-ship / cancel per customer-eligible rule; for high-value/fragile, escalate to Supervisor

fields.Participants: Packers, Quality Checker, Dark Store Shift Supervisor
fields.Trigger: Pick complete; tote arrives at pack station

workflows.name: Pack Station Operations, Quality Check & Right-Box Selection

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-scan of "scans order/tote at pack station" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-validate of "check station validates packed weight vs." (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-log of "logged and fed back to picker/packer accuracy KPI" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-77 (ensure dark-store order accuracy & dispatch control.)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Pack-error risk**: Wrong item or quantity in carton drives returns (links to VS-32) and CS complaints; mitigated by scan-to-pack and weight tolerance
System Touchpoints: - Pack station with display; cartonization/dimensioning; weight-check; quality sampling

steps.activity: Packer scans order/tote at pack station; system displays items expected with images and pack instructions (fragile orientation, hazmat rules — links to VS-24, cold/chemical — links to VS-73); packer scans each item to confirm correctness

System auto-suggests carton size based on cube (dimensioner or item dimensions); packer packs, void-fills, seals; weight-check station validates packed weight vs. expected tolerance; out-of-tolerance orders held for Quality
Quality Checker performs AQL sample audit (e.g., 1 in 50): correct items, quantity, presentation, invoice/packing slip, gift/messages; defects logged and fed back to picker/packer accuracy KPI

fields.Participants: Packers, Inventory/Stores Clerk, Procurement (links to VS-34)
fields.Trigger: Shift start; low-stock alerts; daily consumables plan
fields.Volume: ~300–4,800 cartons consumed/day per dark store (one per order, per W3097's wave volumes) drawn from ~10–20 carton sizes on hand, plus labels, void-fill, tape, ribbons

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-generate of "prints shipping labels and packing slips" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-monitor of "monitors consumables inventory" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-scan of "scan" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-509 (ensure controlled execution — Micro-Fulfillment Daily Pick / Pack / Dispatch Operations (PA-93.2).)
- operational: min/max and dual-source (links to VS-34)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Consumable stockout risk**: Wrong carton size halts pack; mitigated by min/max and dual-source (links to VS-34)
System Touchpoints: - Label/invoice print (links to VS-79); consumables min/max; carrier manifest API (links to VS-56)
Time Estimate: - Continuous; ~30–60 min/day per dark store on consumables mgmt

steps.activity: System prints shipping labels and packing slips (BIR-compliant invoice for the customer's tender — links to VS-79); integrates address validation; applies promotional inserts, return labels, and multi-language instructions per destination

Stores Clerk monitors consumables inventory (cartons by size, void-fill, tape, labels, ribbons, hazmat labels) and replenishes pack stations; min/max triggers replenishment from reserve or procurement via VS-34

Manifest: system builds dispatch manifest per route/carrier/slot; packer loads staged cartons onto dispatch pallet/trolley with manifest scan; system marks orders ready-for-dispatch and notifies carrier/3PL

fields.Frequency: 8–24 dispatch windows per day per dark store
fields.Participants: Dispatch Clerk, 3PL/Rider Partners (links to VS-56), Own Fleet (links to VS-06)
fields.Trigger: Wave packed; dispatch window; carrier pickup
fields.Volume: ~50–500 parcels/load; mix of 3PL rider (last-mile), own-fleet bulk (links to VS-06)

workflows.name: Dispatch Scheduling, Carrier Handoff & Route Consolidation

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-scan of "scans each parcel against manifest" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-route of "Carrier/rider signs for parcels" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-record of "Dispatch Clerk closes manifest, archives signed e-POD to records" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-509 (ensure controlled execution — Micro-Fulfillment Daily Pick / Pack / Dispatch Operations (PA-93.2).)
- operational: multi-carrier SLA (links to VS-56) and surge-rider pool
Pain Points / Risks: - **Carrier no-show / late risk**: Rider/3PL delays break same-day promise; mitigated by multi-carrier SLA (links to VS-56) and surge-rider pool
System Touchpoints: - Manifest/e-POD; carrier API (links to VS-56); TMS (links to VS-06); customer notification (links to VS-10)

steps.activity: Dispatch Clerk confirms carrier/rider arrival; scans each parcel against manifest; system validates route/zone correctness; rejects misrouted parcels back to staging
Carrier/rider signs for parcels (handheld / e-POD); system pushes tracking event to OMS and customer (links to VS-10/VS-13); for own-fleet, TMS route plan (links to VS-06) is loaded to driver app
Dispatch Clerk closes manifest, archives signed e-POD to records (links to VS-88), and reports dispatch KPIs (on-time dispatch, route fill, rider wait time) to Shift Supervisor

fields.Participants: Dark Store Shift Supervisor, Ecommerce Ops (links to VS-60), CS (links to VS-13)
fields.Trigger: Daily operating cycle; cut-off breach; SLA at-risk

workflows.name: Same-Day / Next-Day Delivery Cut-Off & SLA Management

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-validate of "System enforces published cut-offs per zone/promise" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-escalate of "escalates to supervisor/CS to preempt customer complaint" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-log of "apology and remediation" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-509 (ensure controlled execution — Micro-Fulfillment Daily Pick / Pack / Dispatch Operations (PA-93.2).)
- operational: conservative published promise + stretch internal SLA
Pain Points / Risks: - **Promise-creep risk**: Aggressive cut-offs erode customer trust if missed; mitigated by conservative published promise + stretch internal SLA
System Touchpoints: - Cut-off engine (links to VS-10/VS-60); SLA dashboard (links to PA-93.3); CS ticketing (links to VS-13)
Time Estimate: - Continuous; ~1–2 hr/day per dark store on SLA watch

steps.activity: System enforces published cut-offs per zone/promise (e.g., same-day order before 2 PM in Metro Manila Zone 1); auto-extends promise to next tier when cut-off passed; communicates updated promise to customer at checkout (links to VS-10)

Dark Store Shift Supervisor runs SLA watchlist: orders within 30 min of breach flagged red; reprioritizes pick/pack/dispatch, swaps rider/carrier, or escalates to supervisor/CS to preempt customer complaint
CS (links to VS-13) proactively notifies customers of any SLA miss with apology and remediation (credit, loyalty points, free delivery); root-cause feeds into PA-93.3 analytics

fields.Participants: Stage Clerk, Customer Service (links to VS-13), Customer
fields.Trigger: BOPIS order picked; customer ETA; pickup window
fields.Volume: Pick SLA: ready within 4 hr of order (links to VS-10 §8.2); hold 5 days then auto-cancel

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-collect of "collect zone with locker/shelf ID" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-scan of "scans order out, releases goods" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System workflow notification of "For orders approaching 5-day hold" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-509 (ensure controlled execution — Micro-Fulfillment Daily Pick / Pack / Dispatch Operations (PA-93.2).)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Wrong-handover risk**: Releasing to wrong customer drives fraud complaint (links to VS-23); mitigated by ID + pickup code verification
System Touchpoints: - BOPIS staging (links to VS-10); customer notification (links to VS-13/VS-75); refund (links to VS-80); revenue (links to VS-16/VS-17)
Time Estimate: - 2–5 min per handover; aging mgmt daily

steps.activity: Packer stages BOPIS order in dedicated click-and-collect zone with locker/shelf ID; system marks order READY and pushes customer notification (SMS/app — links to VS-13/VS-75) with pickup code/QR

Customer arrives at designated pickup point (dark store counter, partner locker, curbside); Stage Clerk verifies ID/pickup code, scans order out, releases goods; system posts fulfillment and revenue recognition (links to VS-16/VS-17)
For orders approaching 5-day hold: CS proactively contacts customer (links to VS-13); on expiry, auto-cancel, refund, and return inventory to sellable stock (links to VS-32 returns)

fields.Participants: Returns Clerk, Quality, Inventory, CS (links to VS-13), AP/AR
fields.Trigger: Customer returns ecommerce/dark-store order; damaged-in-transit; mis-pick; undeliverable

workflows.name: Dark Store Returns, Reverse Putaway & Exception Handling

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-scan of "Returns Clerk receives returned/undeliverable parcel" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-route of "route to disposition" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-file of "file claim with carrier" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-77 (ensure dark-store order accuracy & dispatch control.)
- operational: inspection, weight check, and serial tracking
Pain Points / Risks: - **Return-fraud risk**: False claims, empty-box returns; mitigated by inspection, weight check, and serial tracking
System Touchpoints: - Returns workflow (links to VS-32); damage/claims (links to VS-90); refunds (links to VS-80); inventory (links to VS-05)

steps.activity: Returns Clerk receives returned/undeliverable parcel; scans order; matches to original shipment; inspects condition (A/B/C/D, saleable/not); logs disposition reason and photos
Quality/Inventory route to disposition: sellable → reverse putaway to pick face (links to VS-05); damaged → damage/claim workflow (links to VS-90); vendor-return → VS-32; dispose → VS-73
Finance/CS process refund (links to VS-80) and any restocking fee per policy; for courier-attributable damage, file claim with carrier (links to VS-56/VS-90); update customer via CS
